route: P2 -> M05 -> Blackwell / bisimulation / information bottleneck
donor_structure: E' sufficient for E iff there is a stochastic garbling matrix G with E = E'G; then E' dominates E in value for EVERY decision problem; bisimulation = maximal equivalence preserving all behavioral queries; IB = maximize I(rep;Y) - beta^-1 I(rep;X)
target_structure: representation rho(Sigma) admissible as a state substitute for the verifier/decision workload
mapping: Sigma <-> experiment; rho <-> coarser experiment; admissibility <-> garbling condition restricted to the verifier's decision set; bisimulation <-> maximal admissible garbling (behavioral queries only); IB <-> burden-priced choice inside the garbling family
preserved_relations: value dominance uniform over decision problems
quotient by a sufficient representation loses nothing for the covered query class
known_broken_relations: for a FINITE query set, strictly weaker-than-Blackwell representations suffice (query-restricted sufficiency); the iff weakens to one direction
IB optimality is Lagrangian/algorithmic (Blahut-Arimoto fixed points), not a closed-form guarantee
unknown_correspondences: whether OCM verifier decision sets are rich enough to force full Blackwell sufficiency (conjecture: yes under adaptive verification)
bisimulation across constitution amendments (moving query set)
assumptions_added: finite decision/action spaces for the garbling matrix form
query set fixed at representation time
candidate_theorem: rho(Sigma) is a sound state substitute iff rho = garbling of Sigma on every query in the verifier's registered decision set; minimal such rho = behavioral quotient
proof_route: parent theorem direct; reduction of 'sound state substitute' to the garbling condition is a restatement, not new mathematics
